title: Streaming Hierarchical Clustering Based on Point-Set Kernel

problem.claim: Hierarchical clustering should provide useful multigranularity structure while handling massive streaming data efficiently.

gap.claim: Existing hierarchical clustering algorithms often lack scalability and the capacity to handle clusters with varying densities because they rely on pairwise point-based similarities that are independent of data distribution.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes StreaKHC, an efficient hierarchical clustering method for mining massive streaming data.
StreaKHC uses a scalable point-set kernel to measure similarity between an existing cluster in the cluster tree and a new streaming point.
StreaKHC includes an efficient mechanism for updating the hierarchical structure in real time.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present StreaKHC as a novel efficient hierarchical clustering method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive empirical evaluation shows StreaKHC is more accurate than existing hierarchical clustering algorithms.
The authors report that extensive empirical evaluation shows StreaKHC is more efficient than existing hierarchical clustering algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hierarchical clustering produces cluster trees at different granularities and provides richer dataset information than partitioning clustering.

Existing hierarchical clustering algorithms face scalability and varying-density limitations associated with pairwise point-based similarity calculations and distribution-independent similarity measures.
The paper introduces StreaKHC for efficient hierarchical clustering of massive streaming data using a scalable point-set kernel.
StreaKHC updates the hierarchical structure efficiently so that a high-quality cluster tree can be maintained in real time.
The authors report higher accuracy and efficiency than existing hierarchical clustering algorithms in extensive empirical evaluation.
